title: SGLang dumper subsystem -- T1059 optional debug port enables sandbox-escape RCE on inference requests
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-15971 (GHSA-h6rf-77vv-9mvj,
CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL), affecting SGLang.

SGLang's optional "dumper" subsystem, activated by setting the
`DUMPER_SERVER_PORT` environment variable, exposes debug/introspection
functionality that allows a sandbox escape reachable through ordinary
inference requests once enabled -- code execution as a side effect of
content the dumper subsystem processes, not a separate authenticated
admin action. Sibling disclosure in the same coordinated research
series as `observed_sglang_lora_adapter_safeunpickler_bypass_rce_t1059`
and `observed_sglang_weights_from_disk_pickle_rce_t1059`; distinct
trigger (an opt-in debug feature) from either.

Detection logic flags the resulting host-observable configuration
state: SGLang running with `DUMPER_SERVER_PORT` set at all, combined
with a listening TCP socket on that port reachable from a
non-loopback origin -- since the vulnerability requires the feature to
be enabled in the first place, its mere activation on a
network-exposed deployment is the actionable signal, independent of
any specific exploitation attempt.

Aggregated from 2 independent sources (SGLang's own GHSA advisory + an
independent security researcher's corroborating disclosure write-up,
part of the same coordinated multi-CVE SGLang research series as the
sibling rules above), no patched version confirmed in the summary
available at authoring time -- operators should disable the dumper
subsystem (unset `DUMPER_SERVER_PORT`) in production unless actively
debugging.
